newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: New Philippine exchange chief vows market reforms.
newsitem.headline: New Philippine exchange chief vows market reforms.

text.p: The new president of the Philippine Stock Exchange pledged on Wednesday to press ahead with reforms such as mechanisms to curb insider trading and the introduction of non-broker board members.
Vitaliano Nanagas, who begins his three-year term next week, told Reuters he would work towards achieving self-regulatory organisation (SRO) status for the exchange.
This would involve installing an effective surveillance system to clamp down on insider trading and price manipulation.

"The PSE itself should be a smoothly-running machine. I'd like them to see a machine that's trying its best to promote investments and build up capital to make enterprises grow," he said in an interview.

Nanagas, a former president of state-owned Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp and an ex-Citibank executive, said by November 12 this year he expects the PSE to be formally granted SRO status by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
"SRO status is like a debut. You're now treated as an adult who can be looked upon to know the consequences of your actions," Nanagas said. The PSE is now regulated by the SEC.
The new stock exchange chief hopes to see more cooperation with the SEC. The PSE and the SEC have clashed several times in what some market analysts have likened to a "turf war."

"The important thing is, we'll be working in the same direction," he said, adding that a mechanism would be in place so that companies issuing shares would not have to grapple with the different requirements of the PSE and the SEC.
Currently, a company has to seek permission from the SEC to sell shares and also go to the PSE to have those shares listed at the exchange.
The bourse will also change its bylaws to include three non-brokers on the 15-member PSE board so that investors will have a voice in the running of the exchange.
In addition, the PSE is expected to confirm this month the creation of a conduct committee to police brokers, Nanagas said, adding that the committee will comprise five brokers.
"It will be a surrogate of the (PSE) board. The five of them will all be brokers to make them responsible ...to put brokers on the spot," he said.
Nanagas also wants to initiate a debate on insider trading. "The definitions are not that clear on insider trading. What is price manipulation? That's the problem," he said.
Other projects that should come into fruition during his term include scripless trading, a board for small and medium-scale enterprises, and derivatives and options trading.
"My job is to liberate or open (the capital markets). I will only question to make sure rules are fair," the PSE head noted.
Nanagas would also like to see more Filipino participation in the exchange, especially by investors outside Manila.
"Getting a good balance of foreign and domestic investors is one of the main priorities," Nangas said. "Right now, the number shows 70-30 in favour of foreigners. It's too lopsided."
"All that in three years. But we'll give our best efforts," he promised.
